blocks.h2: Maintenance for Older and Newer Elmhurst Homes
blocks.body: A 1950s ranch and a 2010 new build need different attention. In the older home, we look closely at the sewer line, galvanized pipe and old shutoff valves. In the newer home, we focus on the water heater, sump and ejector pumps and fixtures that hard water wears down. Either way, a yearly visit means fewer surprises and a clear list of what's coming.

After the visit, you get a short written summary. Each system is marked as fine, worth watching or needing attention, with notes on age and condition. If something needs work, you get a flat price for it. Nothing is done without your approval, and you can schedule repairs when it suits you.

blocks.h2: Plumbing Maintenance Questions From Elmhurst Homeowners

items.q: How often should I flush my water heater?
items.answer: Once a year, given Elmhurst's hard water.

items.q: When should I test my sump pump?
items.answer: In early spring, before the heavy storms. We'll test it as part of the checkup.

items.q: Does the No Drip Club include maintenance?
items.answer: The [No Drip Club](/no-drip-club) includes regular maintenance visits.

items.q: Can you inspect before I sell?
items.answer: Yes. Fixing small issues first helps the buyer's inspection go smoothly.

items.q: Can you check my water pressure?
items.answer: Yes. Pressure that's too high wears out fixtures and appliances.

items.q: Do you check the sewer line during a checkup?
items.answer: We look for warning signs like slow drains and gurgling. If we see any, a camera inspection is the next step.

items.q: Can a checkup lower my insurance risk?
items.answer: It can catch leaks and failing parts before they cause damage. Ask your agent about any discounts for leak sensors.

items.q: How much does plumbing maintenance cost in Elmhurst?
items.preview: It depends on the visit. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on what's included. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
